s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive radicular pain and neuropathic symptoms in the lower extremity
salient_findings: Radicular pain radiating from lower back down the left leg
Mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
Cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone
key_facts: 8-month history of radicular pain
Pain radiates from lower back down the left leg
Occasional tingling
No weakness or autonomic symptoms
No history of trauma or injury
Mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
Normal muscle strength
Negative Lasègue, Kernig, Bragard, and Sicard signs
Electromyography shows neuropathic irritation of left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots
Lumbosacral MRI shows a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone
Mass measures approximately 13.9 cm in length and 1.9 cm in maximal diameter
Mass is hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone, are consistent with a schwannoma, a type of benign nerve sheath tumor.

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's presentation and imaging findings could also be consistent with a neurofibroma, another type of benign nerve sheath tumor, although the lack of multiple lesions or other signs of neurofibromatosis type 1 makes this less likely.

shortlist.label: Tarlov cyst
shortlist.why_kept: The cystic nature of the mass and its location in the nerve root foramen are also consistent with a Tarlov cyst, a type of nerve root cyst that can cause radicular pain and neuropathic symptoms.

shortlist.label: Ganglion cyst
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings could also be consistent with a ganglion cyst, a type of cyst that can occur in the nerve root foramen and cause radicular pain and neuropathic symptoms.

shortlist.label: Plexiform neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, the patient's presentation and imaging findings could also be consistent with a plexiform neurofibroma, a type of benign nerve sheath tumor that can cause neuropathic symptoms and has a more complex, plexiform morphology.

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of radicular pain and the imaging findings of a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone that is hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images, with peripheral rim enhancement, are most consistent with a Tarlov cyst, which is a type of nerve root cyst that can cause nerve irritation and pain.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are typically solid tumors, not cystic, and may show heterogeneous enhancement on MRI.

rejected.label: Neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibromas are also typically solid and may have a more heterogeneous appearance on MRI, with areas of low signal intensity on T2-weighted images.

rejected.label: Ganglion cyst
rejected.why: Ganglion cysts are more commonly associated with joints and tendons, rather than nerve roots, and may not typically cause the same degree of nerve irritation and pain as seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Plexiform neurofibroma
rejected.why: Plexiform neurofibromas are complex, multinodular tumors that involve multiple nerve roots and may have a more extensive and heterogeneous appearance on MRI, which is not consistent with the solitary, cystic mass seen in this patient.
